## Natural history notes

A tiny tortricid moth characterized by narrow tan to brownish forewings with two darker spots or patches and subtle mottled markings typical of many small leafroller relatives. In Florida, it is part of a southeastern to south-central U.S. range and is likely found in open or semi-open habitats with low vegetation, shrubs, or herbaceous host plants. Adults are small, mostly nocturnal, and may come to lights, while the caterpillars likely feed concealed within plant material, flowers, or seed structures, serving as part of the broader food web for spiders, birds, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
